title: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Structured Metadata and Climate Science Publications
title_zh: 由结构化元数据与气候科学出版物驱动的本体引导知识图谱构建

paragraphs.en: The rapid expansion of scientific literature far outpaces the speed of manual curation, creating a fundamental bottleneck in extracting structured knowledge from scientific texts. To address this, we introduce an agentic, ontology-guided framework for knowledge graph (KG) construction. Our framework utilizes specialized agents for document understanding, information extraction, ontology conformance, and entity linking. First, an LLM extracts factual knowledge in the form of triples with explicit textual evidence from research papers. Then the triplets undergo a multistage verification process to ground the triplets in the ontology. By enforcing schema constraints and requiring evidence in the form of text fragments, we ensure the data is both semantically consistent and traceable. In an agreement study over 1,000 extracted triplets, Gemini-2.5-flash achieves Cohen’s κ \kappa scores of 0.640--0.700 against three human annotators, matching the human--human agreement range of 0.616--0.689. We applied this framework to 2,000 scientific publications and construct a novel, ontology-grounded KG for climate science with 133,990 nodes and 755,308 relations; of the 23,327 triplets that the publications contribute after validation, 98.96% are judged correct. The pipeline code and KG is publicly available 1 1 1 https://github.com/aayushacharya/climatekg .
paragraphs.zh: 科学文献的快速扩张远远超出了人工整理的速度，形成了从科学文本中提取结构化知识的根本性瓶颈。 为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种由本体引导的、基于智能体的知识图谱（KG）构建框架。 我们的框架利用专门的智能体来执行文档理解、信息抽取、本体一致性与实体链接。 首先，一个大语言模型从研究论文中以三元组的形式抽取事实知识，并附带明确的文本证据。 随后，这些三元组经过多阶段验证流程，使其与本体相锚定。 通过强制执行模式约束并要求提供文本片段形式的证据，我们确保数据在语义上一致且可追溯。 在一项针对1,000个抽取三元组的一致性研究中，Gemini-2.5-flash 相对于三位人类标注者取得了 0.640--0.700 的 Cohen's κ \kappa 分数，与人类之间 0.616--0.689 的一致性区间相当。 我们将该框架应用于2,000篇科学出版物，构建了一个面向气候科学的、以本体为基础的新型知识图谱，包含133,990个节点和755,308条关系；在经校验后出版物贡献的23,327个三元组中，98.96%被判定为正确。 流水线代码和知识图谱已公开可用 1 1 1 https://github.com/aayushacharya/climatekg 。

paragraphs.en: The volume and complexity of the scientific literature continue to grow at an unprecedented rate Hanson et al. (2024) ; Ding et al. (2025) , challenging the ability of researchers to synthesize knowledge across publications, models, and domains. Knowledge graphs (KGs) provide a structured representation of scientific knowledge that can support semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, and scientific reasoning Peng et al. (2023) ; Guan et al. (2025) . From an NLP perspective, constructing such graphs from unstructured text requires robust information extraction (IE) systems capable of identifying entities, relations, and provenance while respecting domain semantics.
paragraphs.zh: 科学文献的体量与复杂性正以前所未有的速度持续增长 Hanson et al. (2024)；Ding et al. (2025)，这对研究者跨论文、模型与领域综合知识的能力提出了挑战。 知识图谱（KGs）为科学知识提供了一种结构化表示，可以支持语义搜索、检索增强生成与科学推理 Peng et al. (2023)；Guan et al. (2025)。 从自然语言处理（NLP）的视角来看，从非结构化文本构建此类图谱需要强大的信息抽取（IE）系统，能够在遵循领域语义的同时识别实体、关系与来源信息。

paragraphs.en: Recent progress in Large Language Models (LLMs) has significantly improved IE performance Wei et al. (2024) , enabling zero-shot and few-shot extraction of relational facts from scientific text Kartchner et al. (2023) . The large context window of newer LLMs allows the processing of documents without the need to distribute them into chunks. Moreover, the shift from simple text processing to “native” understanding of document layouts, tables, and visual hierarchies without needing separate OCR greatly improves IE Ke et al. (2026) . A parallel line of work has explored ontology-guided IE, where schemas constrain extraction to a fixed set of entity and relation types van Cauter and Yakovets (2024) . Due to semantic consistency and interoperability, ontology-guided methods consistently show better extraction quality in domain specific setting Bhattarai et al. (2024) ; Cotti et al. (2025) .
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）的最新进展显著提升了信息抽取的性能 Wei et al. (2024)，使得从科学文本中零样本和少样本抽取关系事实成为可能 Kartchner et al. (2023)。 较新的LLM拥有较大的上下文窗口，可以处理完整文档而无需将其切分为多个块。 此外，从简单文本处理转向在无需单独OCR的情况下对文档布局、表格和视觉层级进行“原生”理解，极大地改进了信息抽取 Ke et al. paragraphs.en: Climate science exemplifies both the opportunity and the challenge. Recent works Chen et al. (2025) ; Bulian et al. (2024) note that information about climate science is underrepresented in current LLMs. Climate models form the backbone of climate research and assessment, yet critical information about model genealogy, shared components, physical parameterizations, and experimental setups is dispersed across thousands of publications Kuma et al. (2023) . While controlled vocabularies such as Earth System Grid Federation (ESGF), a global infrastructure that standardizes and distributes climate model datasets, and Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6), an international framework defining standardized climate model experiments and metadata, exist, they primarily describe datasets and metadata rather than the rich relational knowledge embedded in the scientific literature. To date, there is very little work done on comprehensive KG integrating these vocabularies with systematically extracted, literature-derived knowledge about climate models, which is the focus of this work.
paragraphs.zh: 气候科学兼具机遇与挑战的典型性。近期的研究 Chen et al. (2025)；Bulian et al. (2024) 指出，当前大语言模型中对气候科学信息的表征不足。 气候模型构成气候研究与评估的支柱，然而关于模型谱系、共享组件、物理参数化方案和实验设置的关键信息却分散在数千篇出版物中 Kuma et al. (2023)。 尽管存在受控词表，例如地球系统网格联邦（ESGF）——一个对气候模型数据集进行标准化和分发的全球性基础设施，以及第六次耦合模型比较计划（CMIP6）——一个定义标准化气候模型实验和元数据的国际框架，但它们主要描述的是数据集和元数据，而非嵌入在科学文献中丰富的关系型知识。 迄今为止，将这些词表与系统性提取的、源自文献的气候模型知识相整合的综合性知识图谱（KG）方面的工作非常少，而这正是本工作的重点。

paragraphs.en: an extraction system must infer that CESM2 and CAM6 are climate models, that the relation corresponds to an ontology-defined predicate such as hasComponent , and that CAM6 represents an atmospheric component rather than a standalone system. Such inferences go beyond surface-level pattern matching and expose a key limitation of open extraction and general-purpose LLMs, which often lack familiarity with specialized climate terminology and its implicit semantics. This motivates the need for ontology-guided extraction that explicitly encodes domain knowledge, constrains relation semantics, and supports reasoning over long-tail scientific entities.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we address these gaps by introducing an evidence-based, ontology-guided IE framework and using it to construct a novel climate KG. Our approach requires each extracted subject–predicate–object triplet to be accompanied by explicit textual evidence and applies automated LLM-based validation to verify both the triplet and its evidence. This design reduces human annotation effort by narrowing manual review to concise evidence spans rather than entire documents, while maintaining high quality through automated filtering. We show that LLM-based validation achieves high agreement with human annotators, enabling scalable KG construction with minimal human intervention. In summary, our contributions are:

paragraphs.en: Climate KG. We introduce a novel climate KG that unifies ESGF metadata with CMIP6 controlled vocabularies, concepts from GCMD (Global Change Master Directory), a NASA-maintained controlled vocabulary that standardizes Earth science metadata to support consistent data discovery and interoperability, and GeoNames-based geolocation. It is further enriched with evidence-grounded relations extracted from 2,000 scientific publications, yielding 133,990 nodes and 755,308 relations that connect models, experiments, variables, institutions, and regions with literature-derived, text-verifiable links; 73,283 of those nodes and 298,747 of those relations come from the publication corpus rather than from the initialization sources.
paragraphs.zh: 气候知识图谱。 我们提出了一种新颖的气候知识图谱，它将 ESGF 元数据与 CMIP6 受控词表、GCMD（全球变化主目录）中的概念以及基于 GeoNames 的地理位置统一起来，其中 GCMD 是由 NASA 维护的受控词表，用于规范地球科学元数据，以支持一致的数据发现与互操作性。 该知识图谱还进一步融入了从 2000 篇科学出版物中抽取的、有证据支撑的关系，共产生 133,990 个节点和 755,308 条关系，将模式、实验、变量、机构和区域以源自文献、可由文本验证的链接连接起来；其中 73,283 个节点和 298,747 条关系来自出版物语料库，而非初始化数据源。

paragraphs.en: Purely open IE suffers from uncontrolled relation phrasing and weak schema alignment, resulting in inconsistent and difficult-to-curate outputs. Ontology-guided extraction mitigates these issues by constraining entity types and relations to a predefined vocabulary and by enforcing semantic consistency through domain and range validation. Recent work has shown that incorporating ontological structure into LLM-based extraction substantially improves relation consistency and downstream usability Nie et al. (2024) .

paragraphs.en: We design a two-level ontology that combines standardized scholarly metadata with domain-specific concepts, using OpenAlex-derived paper-centric entities as a stable backbone. paragraphs.en: We assemble a targeted corpus of domain-specific scientific literature to ensure coverage of authoritative and highly relevant sources. The first phase begins with a small seed set of core papers and expands through two levels of citation mining with LLM-based relevance filtering. After the first phase selected 1,007 papers, we used the top OpenAlex concepts from this set to retrieve recent, context-matched candidates and applied the same screening procedure, adding 993 papers for a 2,000-paper corpus; further details are in Appendix A.1 . The small seed of core papers for climate-domain task was taken from the following sources. The sources were selected on consultation with climate experts: (1) curated references from the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (2023) and (2) CMIP6 publications 1 1 1 https://cmip-publications.llnl.gov/ .

paragraphs.en: To assess whether LLM-based validation can scale KG quality control, we compare Gemini-2.5-flash with three human annotators on 1,000 extracted triplets sampled from IPCC-linked climate-science papers Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (2023) of the corpus of Section 3.2 . The sample is drawn from the raw output of the triplet and evidence extractor agent, before any verification stage, so it contains triplets that the pipeline later keeps as well as triplets it removes. Each decision is the binary judgement of whether the evidence span supports the triplet, which is the task of the validator agent in Figure 1 . As shown in Table 2 , Gemini-human Cohen’s κ \kappa scores range from 0.640–0.700, comparable to the human-human range of 0.616–0.689; against the human majority vote, Gemini reaches κ = 0.798 \kappa=0.798 and 0.977 observed agreement. This supports its use as a scalable surrogate validator for large-scale KG construction.

paragraphs.en: Table 3 shows the effect of each validation stage over 2,000 publications. The extractor produces 39,964 candidate triplets; ontology conformance, evidence validation, and final validation reduce this to 23,327 high-quality triplets with a final correctness score of 98.963%. paragraphs.en: Because every candidate triplet stores the verdict of every stage, we can evaluate all eight combinations of the three verification stages on the same 39,964 triplets with the same C triplet C_{\text{triplet}} judge, without re-running any agent (Table 4 ). The stages act on different axes rather than on a single quality dimension. The validator agent is the precision component: removing it from the full pipeline leaves 27,900 triplets at 94.72%, so it contributes + 4.24 +4.24 points of C triplet C_{\text{triplet}} . Ontology conformance contributes almost no precision, but that is not its function: 93.4% of the 11,050 triplets it removes are judged textually correct, yet their (source type, relation, target type) signature lies outside the ontology, so they cannot be typed into the KG at all. Its role is schema compatibility rather than error correction. Evidence validation likewise leaves final precision unchanged (24,172 at 98.96% without it), and instead supplies the traceability guarantee: without it, 845 triplets whose evidence span cannot be matched against the parsed source enter the KG. Precision, schema compatibility, and traceability therefore have to be read as three separate outcomes of the pipeline. The details about what the pipeline filters remove is given in Appendix A.8 . The verification stack is also inexpensive relative to what it corrects. Appendix A.11 reports cost, runtime, and ablation effect per stage.

paragraphs.en: We further measure knowledge saturation as papers are incrementally linked into the KG. Here, created entities are new KG nodes introduced during entity linking, while mentions are paper-level entity references resolved against the KG. Novelty is computed within each paper interval as the number of unique items not seen in earlier papers divided by the total number of unique items observed in that interval. As shown in Table 1 and Figure 3 , the average number of new unique created entities per paper drops from 16.89 in the first 500 papers to 8.81 in the final 500 papers, while the entity novelty rate drops from 61.9% to 40.3%. Entity mention novelty shows a similar decline, from 43.3% to 24.1%, and relation assertion novelty declines from 84.4% to 73.1%. At the schema level, all 9 created entity types are observed by paper 4, 90% of the final 34 mention entity types are observed by paper 129, and 90% of the final 17 relation types are observed by paper 434. These trends indicate that additional papers increasingly reuse the existing climate KG vocabulary and schema, while continuing to add validated assertions. The same redundancy is visible at the level of individual assertions: of the 6,530 distinct literature-derived edges, 11.0% are asserted independently by two or more papers, and 1.6% by five or more. Facts missed in one paper are therefore often recoverable from overlapping evidence in later papers, which partially mitigates per-document recall limitations at corpus scale.

paragraphs.en: Table 6 compares our framework with KARMA Lu and Wang (2025) , the closest available agentic baseline because it is also a multi-agent framework for extracting KG-style assertions from scientific publications. We are not aware of an existing agentic KG construction system designed specifically for climate-science papers, so we adapt KARMA’s prompts to the climate domain and evaluate both systems on the first 1,007 publications after final validation. Our system extracts 17,141 triplets with 99.067% correctness, while KARMA extracts 3,820 triplets with 92.277% correctness, showing that explicit evidence grounding and ontology-conformance validation improve precision while producing a much larger validated KG.

paragraphs.en: We presented an evidence-based, ontology-guided framework for constructing climate-science KGs from scientific publications. By requiring explicit evidence, validating ontology conformance, and linking entities to a trusted climate KG backbone, the framework produces high-precision, traceable relations at scale. Across 2,000 publications, the pipeline constructs a KG with 133,990 nodes, 755,308 relations, while maintaining high triplet correctness after validation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了一个基于证据、由本体引导的框架，用于从科学出版物中构建气候科学知识图谱。 通过要求明确的证据、验证本体一致性，并将实体链接到可信的气候知识图谱主干，该框架能够大规模地生成高精度、可追溯的关系。 在 2,000 篇出版物上，该流程构建了一个包含 133,990 个节点、755,308 条关系的知识图谱，同时在校验后保持了较高的三元组正确率。

paragraphs.en: The results show that agentic extraction benefits from domain structure: ontology constraints reduce schema drift, evidence validation filters unsupported assertions, and hybrid entity linking connects literature-derived facts to canonical climate entities. Our agreement study supports Gemini-2.5-flash as a scalable validator, and comparisons with KARMA and ClimateIE show that the proposed framework achieves substantially cleaner curator-ready assertions than both a general multi-agent scientific IE baseline and a climate-specific IE baseline. These findings demonstrate the practicality of evidence-centered extraction for constructing auditable, domain-specific scientific KGs.
paragraphs.zh: 结果表明，基于智能体的抽取受益于领域结构：本体约束减少了模式漂移，证据验证过滤了缺乏支持的断言，混合实体链接将文献中抽取的事实与规范的气候实体相连接。 我们的一致性研究支持使用 Gemini-2.5-flash 作为可扩展的验证器，与 KARMA 和 ClimateIE 的比较表明，所提出的框架相较于通用多智能体科学信息抽取基线和气候专用信息抽取基线，都能获得明显更干净、可直接供策展人使用的断言。 这些发现证明了以证据为中心的抽取方法在构建可审计的、领域专用科学知识图谱方面的实用性。

paragraphs.en: Our pipeline performs evidence grounding, ontology checks, entity linking, and validation in addition to extraction. Two of these verification stages are deterministic and the third is a short call to a small model, so the added cost is about 1% of extraction (Appendix A.11 ); the pipeline is nevertheless more expensive than direct extraction, and it inherits the GPU cost of local parsing and screening. We do not compute triplet-level recall, since open-ended scientific text would require exhaustive gold triplets for each document. Instead we report entity-level recall against external curated gold restricted to what the text actually states (90.29% micro-average, Section 4.4 ), and we quantify how many judge-correct triplets each stage removes. These two measurements do not cover relations that no paper in the corpus states explicitly, nor triplets whose entities fall outside the CMIP metadata families. Finally, LLM validators may still over-accept plausible but unstated relations or reject relations requiring dispersed evidence or domain knowledge.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的流水线在抽取之外还执行证据定位、本体检查、实体链接和验证。 其中两个验证阶段是确定性的，第三个只需对一个小模型进行简短调用，因此增加的成本约为抽取成本的1%（附录 A.11）；尽管如此，该流水线仍比直接抽取更昂贵，并且它还继承了本地解析与筛选的GPU成本。 我们不计算三元组级别的召回率，因为开放式的科学文本需要对每篇文档穷尽式地标注黄金三元组。 作为替代，我们针对外部整理的、仅限于文本实际陈述内容的黄金标准报告实体级召回率（微观平均90.29%，第4.4节），并量化每个阶段移除了多少被评判模型判定正确的三元组。 这两项测量既不涵盖语料库中没有论文明确陈述的关系，也不涵盖实体落在CMIP元数据族之外的三元组。 最后，LLM验证器仍可能过度接受看似合理但未被陈述的关系，或拒绝那些需要分散证据或领域知识的关系。

paragraphs.en: We initialize the KG from structured ESGF dataset metadata (see Section 3.4 for the exact snapshot and endpoint), where each record describes a climate simulation using attributes such as experiment identifiers, source model IDs, variables, institutions, and spatial coverage. Dataset-level attributes are deterministically converted into typed ontology entities, while semantic relationships such as usedInExperiment , producesVariable , and coversRegion are instantiated as graph edges. Geospatial bounding boxes are normalized and linked to GeoNames entities, and CMIP6 controlled vocabulary terms are used to enrich model genealogy and component information. The concepts like Ocean circulation, Teleconnection, Instrument and Platform are initialized from GCMD. This initialization grounds later LLM extractions in standardized identifiers; for example, an extracted mention of precipitation can be linked to the canonical ESGF variable pr rather than requiring the LLM to generate the identifier directly.
paragraphs.zh: 我们根据结构化的 ESGF 数据集元数据（确切的数据快照与端点见 3.4 节）来初始化知识图谱（KG），其中每条记录使用实验标识符、源模式 ID、变量、机构以及空间覆盖范围等属性来描述一次气候模拟。 数据集层面的属性被确定性地转换为带类型的本体实体，而诸如 usedInExperiment、producesVariable 和 coversRegion 之类的语义关系则被实例化为图中的边。 地理空间边界框经过规范化处理并链接到 GeoNames 实体，同时使用 CMIP6 受控词汇表术语来丰富模式谱系和组件信息。 诸如海洋环流、遥相关、仪器与平台等概念均从 GCMD 中初始化。 这一初始化过程为后续的大语言模型（LLM）抽取提供了标准化标识符的支撑；例如，抽取到的「降水」提及可以链接到规范的 ESGF 变量 pr，而无需 LLM 直接生成该标识符。

paragraphs.en: Many climate-science statements hold only under a qualifier: an experiment, an ensemble member, a forcing, a region, or a period. We handle these structurally rather than by attaching free-text conditions to a relation. The ontology promotes the qualifier-bearing concepts to first-class entities, so Experiment , SubExperiment , Ensemble , Member , Forcing , Metric , and Result are nodes in their own right, and a conditioned statement is expressed as a path through them instead of as a single qualified edge; the KG contains 35,523 RESULT_HAS_METRIC edges of this form. Evidence spans are stored at paragraph granularity with anaphora resolved, so a qualifier stated next to the claim stays visible to any reader auditing the triple. A statement whose qualifier the ontology cannot express, on the other hand, has no licensed type signature and is removed by the conformance agent rather than entering the KG unconditioned. This is a deliberate trade: it keeps the graph interpretable, and it is one reason the conformance stage removes textually correct triples.
paragraphs.zh: 许多气候科学论断只有在某种限定条件下才成立：某次实验、某个集合成员、某种强迫、某个区域或某个时期。 我们从结构上处理这些条件，而不是将自由文本形式的条件附加到关系上。 本体论将携带限定条件的概念提升为一等实体，因此 Experiment、SubExperiment、Ensemble、Member、Forcing、Metric 和 Result 本身就是节点，而带条件的论断被表示为穿过这些节点的一条路径，而非单一带限定的边；知识图谱中包含 35,523 条这种形式的 RESULT_HAS_METRIC 边。 证据片段以段落粒度存储并完成指代消解，因此写在论断旁的限定条件对任何审核三元组的读者都保持可见。 另一方面，其限定条件无法被本体论表达的论断没有合法的类型签名，会被一致性智能体移除，而不是以无条件的形式进入知识图谱。 这是一个有意的权衡：它保持了图谱的可解释性，也是一致性阶段会移除文本上正确三元组的原因之一。

sents.zh: 本体论将携带限定条件的概念提升为一等实体，因此 Experiment、SubExperiment、Ensemble、Member、Forcing、Metric 和 Result 本身就是节点，而带条件的论断被表示为穿过这些节点的一条路径，而非单一带限定的边；知识图谱中包含 35,523 条这种形式的 RESULT_HAS_METRIC 边。

sents.en: Evidence spans are stored at paragraph granularity with anaphora resolved, so a qualifier stated next to the claim stays visible to any reader auditing the triple.
sents.zh: 证据片段以段落粒度存储并完成指代消解，因此写在论断旁的限定条件对任何审核三元组的读者都保持可见。

sents.en: A statement whose qualifier the ontology cannot express, on the other hand, has no licensed type signature and is removed by the conformance agent rather than entering the KG unconditioned.
sents.zh: 另一方面，其限定条件无法被本体论表达的论断没有合法的类型签名，会被一致性智能体移除，而不是以无条件的形式进入知识图谱。

sents.en: This is a deliberate trade: it keeps the graph interpretable, and it is one reason the conformance stage removes textually correct triples.
sents.zh: 这是一个有意的权衡：它保持了图谱的可解释性，也是一致性阶段会移除文本上正确三元组的原因之一。

paragraphs.en: The same fact is often asserted by several papers, and papers also restate findings that earlier, cited work introduced. Because entity linking resolves mentions to canonical KG nodes, such assertions converge on a single edge rather than on one edge per paper. Each edge accumulates the identifiers of every paper that asserted it in an added_from_paper_id list, and keeps each paper’s evidence span, so the graph records how many independent documents support a relation and which passage each of them offers. In the 2,000-publication KG, 11.0% of the distinct literature-derived edges carry two or more paper identifiers. What the current design does not do is distinguish the paper that introduced a finding from the papers that restate it: a citation-aware provenance model is left for future work.

paragraphs.en: Relative to raw extractor output, the pipeline discards 14,503 triplets that the judge considers correct. Their distribution across stages shows that this is mostly scope filtering rather than a precision–recall trade: 10,326 (71.2%) are removed by ontology conformance and are correct statements whose type signature lies outside the schema, so no ontology-grounded KG could load them; 835 (5.8%) fail evidence grounding, meaning their evidence span cannot be located in the parsed source; and 3,342 (23.0%) are removed by the validator agent, which as shown above rejects unconfirmed rather than only incorrect assertions. Restricting attention to triplets the schema can express, the pipeline retains 23,085 of 27,262 judge-correct triplets, a within-schema retention of 84.7%, while raising C triplet C_{\text{triplet}} from 94.05% to 98.96%. Measured on the human-annotated subset, within-schema retention is 81.9%.

paragraphs.en: The verification stack that follows is close to free. Ontology conformance and evidence validation use no LLM at all: the first is a set-membership test over the licensed (source type, relation, target type) tuples with rule-based normalization, and the second is a fuzzy string match of the evidence span against the parsed document, so both run in CPU minutes at no API cost. The validator agent is the only paid verifier, at one short Gemini-2.5-flash call per surviving triplet: 27,900 calls, approximately 9M input and 0.2M output tokens, or roughly USD 3. Paper screening runs on a locally hosted Llama-3.3-70B and costs GPU time rather than API credit, as does PDF parsing with olmOCR. Entity linking runs local NV-Embed-v2 embeddings and calls an LLM only for candidates that fall in the fallback band [ τ f , τ ) [\tau_{f},\tau) .

paragraphs.en: The entity and relation definitions of the climate ontology are given below.
paragraphs.zh: 气候本体的实体与关系定义如下。

paragraphs.en: Activity : A coordinated modeling effort or scientific campaign.
paragraphs.zh: 活动：一次协调的建模工作或科学行动。

paragraphs.en: ExperimentFamily : A set of climate model experiments conducted under a common scientific objective (e.g., CMIP experiment families).
paragraphs.zh: ExperimentFamily：在共同科学目标下进行的一组气候模式实验（例如 CMIP 实验族）。

paragraphs.en: Experiment : A specific climate model simulation scenario (e.g., historical, ssp585).
paragraphs.zh: Experiment（试验）：一个特定的气候模式模拟情景（例如 historical、ssp585）。

paragraphs.en: SubExperiment : A variant of a climate model experiment with specific configurations (e.g., initialization, ensemble member, or resolution).
paragraphs.zh: SubExperiment：气候模式实验的一种变体，具有特定的配置（例如，初始化、集合成员或分辨率）。

paragraphs.en: Source : A climate model or system used to generate data (e.g., GFDL-ESM4).
paragraphs.zh: 源：用于生成数据的气候模型或系统（例如 GFDL-ESM4）。

paragraphs.en: SourceType : The classification of the model.
paragraphs.zh: SourceType：模型的分类。

paragraphs.en: SourceComponent : A sub-model (e.g., atmosphere, ocean, land) within a coupled climate model; may also function as a standalone model (e.g., ACCESS-OM2).
paragraphs.zh: SourceComponent：耦合气候模式中的一个子模式（例如大气、海洋、陆地）；也可作为独立模式运行（例如 ACCESS-OM2）。

paragraphs.en: PhysicalScheme : A representation of a physical process within a climate model (e.g., cloud scheme).
paragraphs.zh: PhysicalScheme：气候模型中物理过程的表示（例如，云方案）。

paragraphs.en: PhysicalFeature : A structural characteristic of a climate model’s design (e.g., terrain-following grid).
paragraphs.zh: PhysicalFeature：气候模型设计的一种结构特征（例如，随地形变化的网格）。

paragraphs.en: SimulationType : Type of simulation performed (e.g., transient, equilibrium).
paragraphs.zh: SimulationType：执行的仿真类型（例如：瞬态、平衡态）。

paragraphs.en: Metric : Quantitative measure of model performance (e.g., climate sensitivity).
paragraphs.zh: 指标：模型性能的定量度量（例如，气候敏感度）。

paragraphs.en: Project : A broader initiative under which models or experiments are conducted (e.g., CMIP6).
paragraphs.zh: 项目：开展模型或实验所隶属的更广泛的倡议（例如，CMIP6）。

paragraphs.en: Institute : Organization responsible for developing models or running simulations.
paragraphs.zh: Institute：负责开发模型或运行模拟的组织。

paragraphs.en: Variable : Scientific quantities output by models (e.g., temperature, precipitation).
paragraphs.zh: 变量：模型输出的科学量（例如温度、降水）。

paragraphs.en: Realm : Component of the Earth system (e.g., atmosphere, ocean).
paragraphs.zh: 领域：地球系统的组成部分（例如大气、海洋）。

paragraphs.en: Frequency : Temporal resolution of model output (e.g., daily, monthly).
paragraphs.zh: 频率：模型输出的时间分辨率（例如：日、月）。

paragraphs.en: Resolution : Spatial resolution or grid size of the data.
paragraphs.zh: 分辨率：数据的空间分辨率或网格大小。

paragraphs.en: Ensemble : A collection of model runs differing in initial conditions or configurations.
paragraphs.zh: 集合预报（Ensemble）：一组在初始条件或配置上有所不同的模型运行。

paragraphs.en: Member : An individual member of an ensemble.
paragraphs.zh: 成员：合奏团（ensemble）中的一名个体成员。

paragraphs.en: MIPEra : A major generation or version of coordinated experiments (e.g., CMIP5, CMIP6).
paragraphs.zh: MIPEra：协调实验的一个主要世代或版本（例如 CMIP5、CMIP6）。

paragraphs.en: RCM : A regional climate model used for fine-resolution regional simulations.
paragraphs.zh: RCM：一种用于高分辨率区域模拟的区域气候模型。

paragraphs.en: Domain : Geographical coverage of a model.
paragraphs.zh: 领域：模型的地理覆盖范围。

paragraphs.en: Continent : A large continuous landmass (e.g., Asia, Africa).
paragraphs.zh: 大洲：一片巨大的连续陆地（例如：亚洲、非洲）。

paragraphs.en: Country : A sovereign state or territory (e.g., India, USA).
paragraphs.zh: 国家：一个主权国家或地区（例如，印度、美国）。

paragraphs.en: Country_Subdivision : Administrative units within countries (e.g., California).
paragraphs.zh: Country_Subdivision：国家内的行政区划单位（例如，加利福尼亚州）。

paragraphs.en: No_Country_Region : Areas not under country jurisdiction (e.g., open ocean).
paragraphs.zh: No_Country_Region：不受国家管辖的区域（例如，公海）。

paragraphs.en: Instrument : Device used to observe environmental variables (e.g., radiometer).
paragraphs.zh: 仪器：用于观测环境变量的设备（例如辐射计）。

paragraphs.en: Platform : Physical carrier for an instrument (e.g., satellite).
paragraphs.zh: 平台：仪器的物理载体（例如卫星）。

paragraphs.en: Weather_Event : Specific events such as storms or droughts.
paragraphs.zh: Weather_Event : 特定事件，例如风暴或干旱。

paragraphs.en: Teleconnection : Large-scale climate patterns (e.g., ENSO, NAO).
paragraphs.zh: 遥相关：大尺度气候型（例如 ENSO、NAO）。

paragraphs.en: Ocean_Circulation : Movements of ocean waters (e.g., AMOC).
paragraphs.zh: Ocean_Circulation：海洋水的运动（例如 AMOC）。

paragraphs.en: Natural_Hazard : Geophysical events impacting systems (e.g., tsunami, earthquake).
paragraphs.zh: Natural_Hazard：影响系统的地球物理事件（例如，海啸、地震）。

paragraphs.en: NaturalHazardType : The specific type of natural hazard (e.g., Flood, Tornado, Wildfire).
paragraphs.zh: NaturalHazardType：自然灾害的具体类型（例如：洪水、龙卷风、野火）。

paragraphs.en: ClimateZone : Classification of climate based on temperature and precipitation patterns (Tropical, Dry, Temperate, Continental, Polar).
paragraphs.zh: ClimateZone：基于温度和降水模式对气候进行的分类（热带、干燥、温带、大陆性、极地）。

paragraphs.en: INCLUDES_EXPERIMENT : Links an ExperimentFamily to its constituent Experiments.
paragraphs.zh: INCLUDES_EXPERIMENT：将实验族（ExperimentFamily）链接到其包含的各个实验（Experiment）。

paragraphs.en: HAS_SUB_EXPERIMENT : Connects an Experiment to a refining SubExperiment.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_SUB_EXPERIMENT：将一个实验连接到其细化的子实验。

paragraphs.en: IS_OF_TYPE : Connects a Source or Natural_Hazard to its corresponding type.
paragraphs.zh: IS_OF_TYPE：将源（Source）或自然灾害（Natural_Hazard）连接到其对应的类型。

paragraphs.en: APPLIES_TO_REALM : Associates a Source, SourceComponent, or Experiment with a Realm.
paragraphs.zh: APPLIES_TO_REALM：将一个源（Source）、源组件（SourceComponent）或实验（Experiment）与一个领域（Realm）相关联。

paragraphs.en: FOCUSES_ON_REALM : Indicates the Realm emphasized by an Activity.
paragraphs.zh: FOCUSES_ON_REALM : 表示某个「活动」（Activity）所强调的「领域」（Realm）。

paragraphs.en: PARTICIPATED_IN : Connects an Institute to a Project.
paragraphs.zh: PARTICIPATED_IN：将研究所连接到项目。

paragraphs.en: GENERATED_BY_ACTIVITY : Indicates that a Source was produced as part of an Activity.
paragraphs.zh: GENERATED_BY_ACTIVITY：表示某个来源（Source）是作为某个活动（Activity）的一部分而产生的。

paragraphs.en: PRODUCED_BY_INSTITUTE : Links a Source to the responsible Institute.
paragraphs.zh: PRODUCED_BY_INSTITUTE：将来源与负责的研究所相关联。

paragraphs.en: BELONGS_TO_MIP_ERA : Indicates association with a specific MIP Era.
paragraphs.zh: BELONGS_TO_MIP_ERA：表示与特定 MIP Era 的关联。

paragraphs.en: USED_IN_EXPERIMENT : Links a Source or RCM to an Experiment.
paragraphs.zh: USED_IN_EXPERIMENT：将一个来源或 RCM 关联到一个实验。

paragraphs.en: PRODUCES_VARIABLE : Specifies Variables output by a Source or SourceComponent.
paragraphs.zh: PRODUCES_VARIABLE : 指定由源（Source）或源组件（SourceComponent）输出的变量（Variable）。

paragraphs.en: HAS_SUBSEQUENT_VERSION : Links a Source or SourceComponent to a newer version.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_SUBSEQUENT_VERSION：将一个源（Source）或源组件（SourceComponent）链接到一个更新的版本。

paragraphs.en: INHERITED_FROM : Indicates derivation or inheritance between Sources.
paragraphs.zh: INHERITED_FROM：表示各来源（Source）之间的派生或继承关系。

paragraphs.en: HAS_SOURCE_COMPONENT : Connects a Source to its SourceComponents.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_SOURCE_COMPONENT : 将源（Source）连接到其源组件（SourceComponents）。

paragraphs.en: USES_PHYSICAL_SCHEME : Indicates a PhysicalScheme employed by a Source.
paragraphs.zh: USES_PHYSICAL_SCHEME : 表示一个物理方案（PhysicalScheme）被某个源（Source）所采用。

paragraphs.en: HAS_PHYSICAL_FEATURE : Links a Source to a defining PhysicalFeature.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_PHYSICAL_FEATURE : 将一个源（Source）链接到一个定义性的身体特征（PhysicalFeature）。

paragraphs.en: HAS_SIMULATION_TYPE : Connects a Source to a SimulationType.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_SIMULATION_TYPE：将源（Source）连接到仿真类型（SimulationType）。

paragraphs.en: HAS_METRIC : Associates a Source with an evaluation Metric.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_METRIC：将来源（Source）与评估指标（Metric）关联起来。

paragraphs.en: PART_OF_PROJECT : Indicates membership in a Project.
paragraphs.zh: PART_OF_PROJECT : 表示属于某个项目（Project）的成员关系。

paragraphs.en: ASSOCIATED_WITH_MEMBER : Connects a Source to an Ensemble Member.
paragraphs.zh: ASSOCIATED_WITH_MEMBER：将源连接到一个乐团成员。

paragraphs.en: SAMPLED_AT_FREQUENCY : Indicates output Frequency of a Source.
paragraphs.zh: SAMPLED_AT_FREQUENCY：表示源的输出频率。

paragraphs.en: HAS_SPATIAL_RESOLUTION : Specifies the spatial Resolution of an entity.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_SPATIAL_RESOLUTION ：指定实体的空间分辨率。

paragraphs.en: PART_OF_ENSEMBLE : Links a Source or SubExperiment to an Ensemble.
paragraphs.zh: PART_OF_ENSEMBLE：将源或子实验链接到集合体。

paragraphs.en: USES_FORCING : Indicates forcings used in an Experiment.
paragraphs.zh: USES_FORCING : 表示实验（Experiment）中使用的强迫（forcing）。

paragraphs.en: INCLUDES_ENSEMBLE_MEMBER : Connects an Experiment to its Ensemble members.
paragraphs.zh: INCLUDES_ENSEMBLE_MEMBER：将实验与其集合成员连接起来。

paragraphs.en: DRIVEN_BY_SOURCE : Indicates that an RCM is driven by a Source.
paragraphs.zh: DRIVEN_BY_SOURCE : 表示 RCM 由一个源（Source）驱动。

paragraphs.en: COVERS_DOMAIN : Specifies the Domain covered by an RCM or Project.
paragraphs.zh: COVERS_DOMAIN : 指定 RCM 或项目所覆盖的领域（Domain）。

paragraphs.en: MEASURES_VARIABLE : Links an Instrument to the Variable it measures.
paragraphs.zh: MEASURES_VARIABLE：将测量工具（Instrument）与其所测量的变量（Variable）关联起来。

paragraphs.en: MOUNTED_ON : Indicates the Platform carrying an Instrument.
paragraphs.zh: MOUNTED_ON : 表示搭载仪器的平台。

paragraphs.en: PERFORMED_BY_INSTITUTE : Indicates which Institute performed an Experiment.
paragraphs.zh: PERFORMED_BY_INSTITUTE : 表示由哪个研究所执行了某个实验。

paragraphs.en: COVERS_REGION : Specifies the region spanned by an RCM.
paragraphs.zh: COVERS_REGION：指定由一个 RCM 所覆盖的区域。

paragraphs.en: IMPACTED_REGION : Indicates the region affected by a Weather_Event.
paragraphs.zh: IMPACTED_REGION : 表示受 Weather_Event 影响的区域。

paragraphs.en: INFLUENCES_REGION : Links a Teleconnection to influenced regions.
paragraphs.zh: INFLUENCES_REGION : 将遥相关连接到受影响的区域。

paragraphs.en: OBSERVED_IN_REGION : Indicates regions where an Ocean_Circulation is observed.
paragraphs.zh: OBSERVED_IN_REGION：表示观测到海洋环流（Ocean_Circulation）的区域。

paragraphs.en: AFFECTED_REGION : Indicates regions affected by a Natural_Hazard.
paragraphs.zh: AFFECTED_REGION：表示受自然灾害（Natural_Hazard）影响的区域。

paragraphs.en: IN_CONTINENT : Connects a Country to its Continent.
paragraphs.zh: IN_CONTINENT : 将国家与其所在的大陆连接起来。

paragraphs.en: IN_COUNTRY : Connects a Country_Subdivision or City to its Country.
paragraphs.zh: IN_COUNTRY：将 Country_Subdivision 或 City 连接到其所属的 Country。

paragraphs.en: HAS_CLIMATE_ZONE : Links a No_Country_Region to a ClimateZone.
paragraphs.zh: HAS_CLIMATE_ZONE : 将 No_Country_Region（非国家区域）链接到一个 ClimateZone（气候区）。

paragraphs.en: Paper : A scholarly publication that reports research contributions, methods, experiments, and results.
paragraphs.zh: Paper（论文）：报告研究贡献、方法、实验与结果的学术出版物。

paragraphs.en: Field : A broad research area or discipline to which a paper contributes (e.g., information retrieval, computer vision).
paragraphs.zh: 字段：论文所属的一个宽泛的研究领域或学科（例如：信息检索、计算机视觉）。

paragraphs.en: Problem : A specific research challenge or question that the paper aims to address.
paragraphs.zh: 问题：论文旨在解决的特定研究挑战或问题。

paragraphs.en: Method : A technical approach, algorithm, or procedure proposed or applied to solve a problem.
paragraphs.zh: 方法：为解决某一问题而提出或应用的技术途径、算法或流程。

paragraphs.en: Innovation : A novel idea, contribution, or improvement introduced by the paper relative to prior work.
paragraphs.zh: 创新：指该论文相对于先前工作所提出的新颖想法、贡献或改进。

paragraphs.en: Task : A well-defined computational or scientific objective used to evaluate methods (e.g., classification, forecasting).
paragraphs.zh: 任务：用于评估方法（如分类、预测）的明确定义的计算或科学目标。

paragraphs.en: Venue : The conference, journal, or workshop where the paper is published.
paragraphs.zh: 发表场所：论文所发表的会议、期刊或研讨会。

paragraphs.en: Author : An individual who contributed intellectually to the creation of the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 作者：对论文的创建做出智力贡献的个人。

paragraphs.en: Keyword : A salient term or phrase summarizing key topics or concepts of the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 关键词：一个概括论文关键主题或概念的显著术语或短语。

paragraphs.en: ObservationalDataset : A dataset used for experimentation or evaluation, typically derived from real-world or empirical observations.
paragraphs.zh: ObservationalDataset（观测数据集）：用于实验或评估的数据集，通常来源于真实世界或经验性观测。

paragraphs.en: Metric : A quantitative measure used to evaluate the performance or quality of a method or model.
paragraphs.zh: 指标：一种用于评估方法或模型性能或质量的定量测量手段。

paragraphs.en: Result : An experimental outcome or reported finding, often associated with a metric value.
paragraphs.zh: 结果：一个实验性的结果或报告的发现，通常与一个度量值相关联。

paragraphs.en: The scientific-publication ontology contains paper-level relations for venue, authorship, keywords, model use, metrics, results, and paper mentions; method- and task-level relations for problems, innovations, tasks, metrics, observational datasets, and results; model- and result-level relations for observational datasets, metrics, and reported results; and LLM-extracted ontology-aligned relations stored with provenance ( added_from_paper_id ).
paragraphs.zh: 科学出版物本体包含论文级关系，涵盖期刊、作者身份、关键词、模型使用、指标、结果和论文引用；方法级和任务级关系，涵盖问题、创新点、任务、指标、观测数据集和结果；模型级和结果级关系，涵盖观测数据集、指标和报告的结果；以及带有溯源信息（ added_from_paper_id ）存储的由大语言模型抽取的与本体对齐的关系。

paragraphs.en: In order to benefit from established scientific terminology and ensure interoperability with existing climate data infrastructures, our domain ontology is constructed by unifying multiple authoritative sources of climate terminology. Specifically, we integrate standardized climate model names, institutions, experiments, and variables from ESGF metadata 1 1 1 https://esgf.github.io/ and the GCMD taxonomy defined in Pan et al. (2025b) , which together provide vetted, community-accepted identifiers and a widely adopted semantic taxonomy for Earth system science. To capture internal model structure and configuration details that are not explicitly represented in ESGF metadata, we further incorporate climate model component information from the CMIP6 Controlled Vocabulary repository 2 2 2 https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/CMIP6_CVs , enabling canonical representation of model components and experiments. Finally, to provide unambiguous spatial grounding, geographic entities such as regions and countries are linked to GeoNames identifiers, supporting spatially contextualized relations (e.g., model evaluation over specific regions) and facilitating integration with external KGs that rely on standardized geographic identifiers.
paragraphs.zh: 为了受益于既有的科学术语体系，并确保与现有气候数据基础设施的互操作性，我们的领域本体通过统一多个权威的气候术语来源构建而成。 具体而言，我们整合了来自 ESGF 元数据 1 1 1 https://esgf.github.io/ 的标准化气候模式名称、机构、实验与变量，以及 Pan 等人定义的 GCMD 分类体系。 (2025b)，它们共同为地球系统科学提供了经过审核、被社区认可的标识符，以及一个被广泛采用的语义分类体系。 为了捕捉 ESGF 元数据中未显式表示的模式内部结构与配置细节，我们进一步纳入了来自 CMIP6 受控词汇表仓库 2 2 2 https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/CMIP6_CVs 的气候模式分量信息，从而实现对模式分量与实验的规范化表示。 最后，为了提供无歧义的空间定位，区域、国家等地理实体被关联到 GeoNames 标识符，从而支持空间情境化的关系（例如针对特定区域的模式评估），并便于与依赖标准化地理标识符的外部知识图谱进行整合。

paragraphs.en: The ontology conformance agent is fully deterministic: it uses no LLM, no external reasoner, and no learned component. The curated ontology is compiled into a set ℒ \mathcal{L} of 35 licensed tuples (source type, target type, relation), and a triple conforms if and only if it passes both of the following tests.
paragraphs.zh: 本体符合性智能体是完全确定性的：它不使用大语言模型、不使用外部推理器，也不使用任何学习组件。 精选本体被编译为一个集合 ℒ \mathcal{L}，其中包含 35 个许可三元组（源类型、目标类型、关系），当且仅当一个三元组同时通过以下两项测试时，它才符合规范。

paragraphs.en: The test is a constant-time set lookup after case and whitespace normalization of the type names. For example, (Source, SourceComponent, HAS_SOURCE_COMPONENT) is licensed, whereas the reversed extraction (SourceComponent, Source, HAS_SOURCE_COMPONENT) is not, which is the case discussed in Section 3.3 . Licensing is what makes relation direction and argument order enforceable without asking a model to check them.
paragraphs.zh: 该测试是在对类型名称进行大小写和空白符归一化之后的一次常数时间集合查找。 例如，(Source, SourceComponent, HAS_SOURCE_COMPONENT) 是获得许可的，而反向抽取得到的 (SourceComponent, Source, HAS_SOURCE_COMPONENT) 则不是，这正是第 3.3 节所讨论的情况。 正是许可机制使得关系方向和参数顺序无需依赖模型检查即可得到强制执行。

paragraphs.en: We assess the factual reliability of LLM-extracted evidence by verifying it against the original PDF content parsed using the Olmocr v2 Poznanski et al. (2025) parser. For each extracted triple, the associated evidence span generated by the LLM is aligned with the parsed PDF text. An evidence instance is considered correct if the cited text can be unambiguously located in the parsed content and faithfully supports the extracted relation; otherwise, it is marked as a hallucination.
paragraphs.zh: 我们通过将LLM提取的证据与使用Olmocr v2解析器（Poznanski et al., 2025）解析的原始PDF内容进行比对，来评估其事实可靠性。 对于每个提取的三元组，将LLM生成的相关证据片段与解析后的PDF文本进行对齐。 如果所引用的文本能够在解析内容中被明确定位，并且忠实地支持所提取的关系，则该证据实例被视为正确；否则，该实例将被标记为幻觉。

sents.zh: 我们通过将LLM提取的证据与使用Olmocr v2解析器（Poznanski et al., 2025）解析的原始PDF内容进行比对，来评估其事实可靠性。

paragraphs.en: For each extracted triple, the extractor also outputs a supporting evidence span. We compute the textual similarity between the extracted evidence span and the source document using the RapidFuzz library. RapidFuzz provides normalized string-matching scores in the range [ 0,100 ] [0,100] , where higher values indicate stronger lexical overlap. In our experiments, a triple is considered evidence-grounded if its similarity score exceeds a predefined threshold (70%, 75%, or 80%). Triples failing this criterion are flagged as hallucinations.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个抽取出的三元组，抽取器还会输出一个支持性证据片段。 我们使用 RapidFuzz 库计算抽取的证据片段与源文档之间的文本相似度。 RapidFuzz 提供范围在 [0,100] 内的归一化字符串匹配分数，分数越高表示词汇重叠越强。 在我们的实验中，如果三元组的相似度分数超过预定义的阈值（70%、75% 或 80%），则认为该三元组有证据支撑。 未通过该标准的三元组被标记为幻觉。

paragraphs.en: Table 12 reports results when all evidence spans are considered (including those derived from tables and figures), hallucination rates range from 7.74 % 7.74\% at an 80 % 80\% threshold to 6.14 % 6.14\% at a 70 % 70\% threshold. As expected, relaxing the similarity threshold admits more borderline matches and thus reduces the measured hallucination rate.

paragraphs.en: Annotators are tasked with validating extracted knowledge graph triples with respect to their supporting textual evidence. Given the relatively lightweight nature of this task, annotators are not required to perform open-ended information extraction or domain discovery. Instead, they are provided only with the ontology definitions, including entity types and relation descriptions, to guide consistent judgments.

paragraphs.en: For each candidate triple, annotators are shown: (i) the structured triple, (ii) the corresponding evidence paragraph extracted from the source document, and (iii) the relevant ontological definitions. Annotators are instructed to verify whether the evidence explicitly supports the triple and whether the triple conforms to the ontology’s domain and range constraints. No additional domain expertise beyond the provided definitions is assumed, and annotators are not asked to infer unstated facts or resolve ambiguities beyond the given text.

paragraphs.en: Title: Triplet and evidence extractor agent prompt Input: PDF in native format(not parsed), ontology, entity_definitions, relation_definitions Output: Structured format: List of source entity class, source entity instance, relation, target entity class, target entity instance Role Description: You are an expert in extracting information from scientific papers. Your job is to answer the user’s query based on the pdf file you have access to. Task: You are given a scientific paper (or paragraph from it) related to climate modeling or Earth system science. The KG is primarily composed of ESGF metadata. Your task is to extract (source, relation, target) triplets with type that match the ontology below. For each extracted triplet, provide all supporting paragraphs from the text and explicitly resolve any anaphoras (e.g., "it", "this model") into their full entity names. The ontology is given below in the form of (source type, target type, relation): Ontology: {ontology} Sample ontology: (’SourceComponent’,’Variable’,’PRODUCES_VARIABLE’) (’SourceComponent’,’Realm’,’APPLIES_TO_REALM’) (’Source’,’PhysicalScheme’,’USES_PHYSICAL_SCHEME’) Entity type definitions: {entity_definitions} Sample definitions: Source: A climate model or system used to generate data (e.g., GFDL-ESM4). SourceComponent: A sub-model (e.g., atmosphere, ocean, land) within a coupled climate model. It may also function as a standalone climate model when used independently (e.g., ACCESS-OM2 as the ocean component in ACCESS-CM2). Realm: Component of the Earth system (e.g., atmosphere, ocean). Variable: Scientific quantities output by models (e.g., temperature, precipitation). PhysicalScheme: A representation of a physical process within a climate model (e.g., cloud scheme). Relation definitions: {relation_defintions} Sample definitions: PRODUCES_VARIABLE: Specifies that a Source or SourceComponent outputs a particular Variable. APPLIES_TO_REALM: Indicates that a Source, SourceComponent, or Experiment is associated with a specific Realm (e.g., atmosphere, ocean, land surface). USES_PHYSICAL_SCHEME: Indicates that a Source employs a particular PhysicalScheme (e.g., radiation scheme, convection scheme). ONLY PROVIDE THE TRIPLETS IF THEY ARE PRESENT IN THE PAPER.
paragraphs.zh: 标题：三元组与证据抽取智能体提示词 输入：原生格式（未解析）的 PDF、本体、实体定义、关系定义 输出：结构化格式：由源实体类、源实体实例、关系、目标实体类、目标实体实例组成的列表 角色描述：你是从科学论文中抽取信息的专家。 你的工作是根据你可以访问的 PDF 文件回答用户的查询。 任务：你会得到一篇与气候建模或地球系统科学相关的科学论文（或其中的一段）。 知识图谱主要由 ESGF 元数据组成。 你的任务是抽取（源，关系，目标）三元组，其类型须与下方的本体相匹配。 对于每个抽取的三元组，请提供文中所有支持该三元组的段落，并将所有指代（例如“它”“该模型”）显式解析为完整的实体名称。 本体以下方（源类型，目标类型，关系）的形式给出：本体：{ontology} 本体示例：（’SourceComponent’,’Variable’,’PRODUCES_VARIABLE’）（’SourceComponent’,’Realm’,’APPLIES_TO_REALM’）（’Source’,’PhysicalScheme’,’USES_PHYSICAL_SCHEME’） 实体类型定义：{entity_definitions} 定义示例：Source：用于生成数据的气候模型或系统（例如 GFDL-ESM4）。 SourceComponent：耦合气候模型中的子模型（例如大气、海洋、陆地）。 当独立使用时，它也可以作为独立的气候模型运行（例如作为 ACCESS-CM2 中海洋分量的 ACCESS-OM2）。 Realm：地球系统的组成部分（例如大气、海洋）。 Variable：模型输出的科学量（例如温度、降水）。 PhysicalScheme：气候模型中某一物理过程的表示（例如云方案）。 关系定义：{relation_defintions} 定义示例：PRODUCES_VARIABLE：表示某个 Source 或 SourceComponent 输出某个特定的 Variable。 APPLIES_TO_REALM：表示某个 Source、SourceComponent 或 Experiment 与特定的 Realm 相关联（例如大气、海洋、陆地表面）。 USES_PHYSICAL_SCHEME：表示某个 Source 采用某个特定的 PhysicalScheme（例如辐射方案、对流方案）。 仅当三元组确实出现在论文中时才提供它们。
